result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_aperiodic()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a strongly connected directed graph is aperiodic. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L46232-L46308){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_aperiodic() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is aperiodic](/assets/graphs/is-aperiodic.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: the directed cycle A, B, C, D plus the chord C to A, which closes the 3-cycle A, B, C (accent color) beside the 4-cycle; the cycle lengths 3 and 4 have greatest common divisor 1, so is_aperiodic() returns True. Right: the 4-cycle alone has only cycles of length 4, so its period is 4 and is_aperiodic() returns False; the dashed chord marks the missing edge." width="100%"} The period of a strongly connected directed graph is the greatest common divisor of the lengths of all its cycles; the graph is aperiodic when that divisor is 1. A random walk (Markov chain) on a strongly connected graph converges to a unique stationary distribution from any start exactly when the graph is aperiodic, which is why PageRank and MCMC samplers care about it: a bipartite-like cycle structure makes the walk oscillate instead of settling. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph is aperiodic. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected, empty, or not strongly connected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A breadth-first search assigns levels; the period divides `level(u) - level(v) + 1` for every edge `u -> v`, and the greatest common divisor of those values over all non-tree edges is the period (Jarvis and Shier, 1996), $O(V + E)$. Matches NetworkX's `is_aperiodic`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A directed 4-cycle has period 4; adding a chord that closes a 3-cycle makes the period gcd(3, 4) = 1: ::: {#049d9a8a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec ring = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) ring.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A")]) before = ring.is_aperiodic() ring.add_edge("C", "A") before, ring.is_aperiodic() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (False, True) ``` ::: :::
